text:
ConocoPhillips fell nearly 0.4% today to $127.02, extending a steep 5.9% drop over two weeks. The immediate driver is the sharp decline in crude oil prices: US oil has tumbled to $107 per barrel, down from much higher levels just days ago, after Trump signaled openness to talks with Iran and indicated a potential diplomatic path forward. Oil prices reversed their early gains on the back of this news, taking energy stocks down with them—refiners and producers make less money when crude gets cheaper.

The deeper context is pure uncertainty. Wall Street analysts have admitted they don't know where oil is heading given the shifting geopolitical situation around Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, and Ukraine. That kind of fog—where the price could swing sharply depending on which headline breaks next—tends to pressure energy stocks as investors wait for clarity rather than commit.
